checks.name: 30-unit program
checks.quote: The M.S. Computer Science degree program is 30 units equivalent to 10 courses. Of these, 5 courses (15 units) are required by all students in the program, 4 courses (12 units) are elective courses, and once course is a capstone experience (3-6 units).

checks.name: Three concentrations
checks.quote: When you apply you will be asked to select a concentration. We currently have three concentrations that allow specialization in a particular area.

checks.name: Typical load
checks.quote: Students enrolled in the M.S. graduate program typically take 1-4 courses (3-12 units) each semester, depending on their situation.

checks.name: Admissions review path
checks.quote: After the Office of Admissions has completed their review, applications are forwarded to the Computer Science department which makes the decision whether to accept or reject the applicant.

checks.name: GRE required on start page
checks.quote: GRE general test scores are required.

checks.name: GRE no longer required on prospective page
checks.quote: Please note: GRE scores are no longer required.

checks.name: Undergraduate GPA 3.0
checks.quote: must have a grade point average of 3.0 in all undergraduate work, and must have earned a "B" or better in the Computer Science and Mathematics courses listed below.

checks.name: Preferred B+ in important courses
checks.quote: Currently, to be eligible for admission into the M.S. program, we prefer at least a B+ average in the important courses.

checks.name: International class standing
checks.quote: For international applicants, we look for students who have graduated first class or first class with distinction.

checks.name: Conditional admission
checks.quote: may be admitted to the program at the discretion of the department as a "Conditionally Classified Graduate" student, provided the student's record clearly demonstrates the capability of completing all the course requirements after admission.

checks.name: Deficiency grades on start page
checks.quote: Students must complete any course deficiencies or remediation with grades of "B" or better. Course deficiencies or remediation must be completed before enrolling in graduate Computer Science courses.

checks.name: Prerequisite grade on first-year page
checks.quote: Each prerequisite must be passed with a B− or better and does not count toward the MS degree.

checks.name: Most students conditionally classified
checks.quote: Nearly all incoming students are admitted as Conditionally Classified, which means your admission letter lists prerequisite or remediation courses to complete in addition to your graduate coursework.

checks.name: Lower-division CS prerequisites
checks.quote: CS 101 Computer Science I

checks.name: Upper-division CS prerequisites
checks.quote: CS 301 Data Structures and Algorithms

checks.name: Math prerequisites
checks.quote: MATH 130 Calculus I

checks.name: Junior college limit
checks.quote: Courses from junior colleges can be used to fulfill lower division admission prerequisites (100 and 200 level) but not upper division admission prerequisites (300 or 400 level.)

checks.name: Open University note
checks.quote: While Open University allows students to take courses before being accepted to the Master's program, Open University students have the last registration priority and no student visa are sponsored by the Open University program.

checks.name: Graduate GPA
checks.quote: The MS in Computer Science requires 30 units of 600-level coursework, each passed with a C or better and an overall 3.0 graduate GPA.

checks.name: Five required core courses
checks.quote: Every student completes five required core courses: CS 601, CS 611, CS 621, CS 651, and CS 671.

checks.name: Capstone options
checks.quote: You also complete a concentration and a capstone — the Comprehensive Exam (CS 692), a Project (CS 693), or a Thesis (CS 699).

checks.name: CS 692 eligibility
checks.quote: and have a cumulative GPA of 3.0.

checks.name: CS 692 attempts
checks.quote: CS 692 Capstone Exams is a three (3) unit class. Grading is CR/NC. Students need to pass all three exams to earn a credit for the class.

checks.name: CS 693 GPA
checks.quote: In addition, the student must have a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or higher.

checks.name: CS 699 GPA
checks.quote: In addition, the student must have a graduate course GPA and cumulative CSUEB GPA of 3.5 or higher.

checks.name: Pay fees by the deadline
checks.quote: Pay your fees by the deadline — even if you are waitlisted. Unpaid fees can drop you from all classes.

checks.name: International full-time enrollment
checks.quote: International (F-1) students must enroll in at least 8 units each fall and spring.

checks.name: Financial aid and prerequisites
checks.quote: Because prerequisites are undergraduate courses that do not count toward the degree, enrolling in prerequisites alone — even a full load — does not establish aid eligibility.
